Registration class, and what the vendor actually sells. Three readings of 'ISP proxy' were considered. (1) Addresses physically hosted on consumer ISP lines - refuted by the vendor's own sentence that they 'originate from datacenter proxies'. (2) Datacenter-hosted addresses announced from an ISP's own ASN, which is what the page describes and what makes a target see a residential registration - confirmed by that sentence together with 'Premium ASN providers' and the named ASNs. (3) A marketing synonym for a datacenter proxy with no technical difference - not excluded, because the vendor publishes no ASN or hosting-provider list per address; what would settle it is a paid account, one address, and a lookup of the announcing ASN plus a traceroute showing a datacenter hop. The record therefore states the class the vendor claims and does not claim the addresses are consumer-hosted. One sample: the sentence read is the vendor's own description of the product, not a measurement of any address.

Two source corrections. First, the blocklist is not on the ISP pages: the pricing and product pages for ISP proxies and static residential were each fetched and grepped for 'restricted on our' and returned zero matches, while the residential pricing page carries the full sentence. The record cites that page. Second, the products/isp-proxies page title advertises 'from $2.10/IP' while the pricing table's smallest band is USD 1.50/IP; the table is used because it carries the band structure, and the headline is recorded in extras as a discrepancy rather than resolved.

Corrects a neighbouring record's emphasis. dossier/debrid/oxylabs.json records identity_cost.kind 'card' with the detail 'Self-service subscription with card', and records the USD 5 welcome credit as its free tier. This record finds the two gates are separate: the credit is claimed with an email and no card is stated for it, while the card belongs to the plan. That does not make the debrid record wrong about the subscription it prices, but its 'card' describes the paid plan and not the way in, and a reader who took it as the credit's cost would overstate the entry price.

Interface vocabulary conflict, unresolved and named rather than hidden. scripts/dossier/schema.json enumerates interface items as s3, s3-compatible, rest, graphql, webdav, sftp, ftp, ftps, scp, rsync, smb, nfs, ssh, graph, oci, git, rclone, cli, webdav-proxy, nntp, unknown. It has no http-proxy and no socks5, so a record using either fails validate.py with an enum error - checked by running the validator on a copy carrying both tokens. This record uses 'rest', the token common to the schema and to the proxy vocabulary, and puts the protocols, the endpoint and the port scheme in interface_detail so nothing is lost. At the gate run on 2026-10-24, dossier/ip-proxy/decodo-isp-proxies.json and dossier/ip-proxy/openproxylist-xyz.json use 'socks5', 'http-proxy' and 'web-ui' and are the four enum errors the schema check reports; eleven of the topic's twenty-one records use 'rest' for the reason this one does. Adding the two proxy tokens to the enum is a two-line change and would let every ip-proxy record say what it is.
